Overview

PT PMA is the form a foreign-owned company takes in Indonesia, licensed through the OSS risk-based system and subject to the investment ministry's capital and business-field rules.

Apostille or consular legalisation of Indian documents — passports, address proofs, board resolutions — is usually needed and takes time to arrange. Bank account opening is often slower than incorporation itself, because banks run their own due diligence on the owners and the expected transactions. Entities formed abroad by Indian founders without the ODI reporting in place are the most common problem we are asked to fix later, and regularising them takes longer than doing it at the start.

Who this applies to

  • An Indian company opening a sales entity close to its customers
  • A foreign company setting up its presence in India
  • A group restructuring its overseas holdings

Documents required

  • Passport of every director and shareholder
  • Indian-side documents for the ODI filing — valuation, board approval, bank forms
  • Source-of-funds information for the bank and the agent's due diligence
  • Proposed company name and business activity

How the filing proceeds

  1. 1

    Applicability check

    We confirm that this is the right registration for what you do, and whether anything else must be in place before it can be filed.

  2. 2

    Application filed

    The application is submitted on the registry's filing system and the acknowledgement shared with you.

  3. 3

    Queries and grant

    Any clarification the department raises is answered on your behalf until the certificate of incorporation is issued.

Questions people ask

Most overseas investments by Indian residents fall under the automatic route of the FEMA overseas investment framework and are reported through the AD bank rather than approved in advance, but the route, limits and documents depend on who is investing and how.

Generally the company needs a bank account in its own name, usually in its own jurisdiction or with an international bank. That account is often the step that takes longest.

Often, but where the company is managed and controlled affects its tax residence. A foreign company effectively managed from India can be treated as resident in India for tax.

It can be started, but filing with a missing or mismatched document is the most common reason for a query or rejection. We hold the filing until the set is complete.
